To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the comprehension of written sentences about object-related hand actions is associated with the activation of both a functional action representation and a volumetric one.

(1) both functional and volumetic hand actions are evocked during sentence comprehension, (2) functional hand actions are selected over volumetric hand actions when the sentence is followed by a picture, and (3) the time course of the two action representations is the same when a picture is presented alone.
the comprehension of written sentences about hand actions involves the evocation of motor programs for both functional and volumetic hand actions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the nature of the motor representations evoked by written sentences.
the question of whether and how the comprehension of language involves the evocation of motor actions.
the question whether and when language processing involves activation of motor representations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
motor representations are evoked during sentence comprehension, but that their nature depends on the context of the sentence.
the motor system is involved in sentence processing and that this involvement is context-dependent.
the motor system is activated during sentence processing, but that the nature of the motor activation depends on the type of task and context.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the evoked motor representations are context-dependent and are modulated by the context.
the motor system is activated by language, but that this activation does not always result in context-specific motor imagery.
the evocation of motor information is not restricted to the processing of action verbs, but also occurs during processing of other words in the sentence, such as nouns.
The main takeaway from our work is that
action representations are evoked during sentence comprehension, but their evocation is not necessarily context-sensitive.
the evocation of motor action representations is not restricted to the processing of sentences that explicitly mention an action.
the motor system is involved in the comprehension of sentences describing object-related hand actions.
